live.name: MageCart
live.headline: MageCart: a threat actor listed in the MISP galaxy
live.in_short: MageCart is listed in the MISP galaxy catalogue. The record gives no aliases and no tools. No public report in this library describes its operations.

sentences.t: MageCart is a threat actor named in the MISP galaxy catalogue.
The catalogue record lists no aliases and no tools for it.
No public report in this library describes its operations.

next.name: MageCart
next.headline: MageCart: the card-skimming operations that hide script code in online checkout pages
next.in_short: MageCart is a name for web card skimming. Malicious JavaScript on checkout pages copies card details. Several groups use it, and reports describe victims from airlines to campus stores.

sentences.t: Malpedia describes Magecart as a malware framework meant to steal credit card information from compromised eCommerce websites.
Trend Micro says multiple groups are using the Magecart code, which it describes as a piece of malicious JavaScript.
Malpedia's reference list carries headlines naming Magecart Group 4, Group 8, Group 12 and a group called Keeper.
eSentire says FIN7 is one of many cyber gangs observed taking part in Magecart attacks.
WIRED says Magecart hackers cast the widest possible net to find vulnerable ecommerce sites.
WIRED also says Magecart has been behind some of the bigger hacks of recent years, from British Airways to Ticketmaster.
Trend Micro points to online campus stores serving nearly 200 universities in the US and Canada.
One headline in Malpedia's list reports campaigns that infected 311 restaurants through online ordering platforms.

ANY.RUN reports a long-running campaign that mostly hit retail e-commerce companies, with victims in at least 12 countries, concentrated in Spain, France and the United States. It says banks, not merchants, bear the primary impact.
Malpedia says the first stage is typically JavaScript on a compromised checkout page, which sends card data to command and control servers.

Trend Micro lists three tactics: infecting third-party companies that supply code to other sites, scanning the internet for unsecured servers, and writing skimming code that works across many payment pages.
One report says most Magecart attacks happen when hackers use vulnerabilities in self-hosted stores to plant skimmer code.
Malwarebytes found skimmers hosted on Heroku. A rogue iframe overlays the real payment form, and stolen data goes back in encoded form.
ANY.RUN describes a campaign that imitated payment pages and sent card data out over WebSocket.
A Malpedia headline says Magecart groups abuse Google Tag Manager.

RiskIQ reports that Magecart operators registered a lookalike domain on August 13th, 2018. It says the skimmer on Newegg's payment page became active around August 14th and was removed on September 18th.
RiskIQ says the Newegg skimmer code is recognisable from the British Airways incident.
WIRED reported in July 2019 that the group had hit 17,000 domains in a few months.
In October 2019, hackers breached Volusion, a cloud-hosted store provider. The report says more than 6,500 stores were affected and calls it a Magecart-style supply-chain attack.
Malwarebytes reported skimmers on Heroku in December 2019 and says the abusive instances were reported and taken down.
ANY.RUN reports a campaign active for at least 24 months and supported by over 100 domains.
Shop owners should review every script that loads on their checkout pages and investigate any they do not recognise.
